Order No. 08 Dated- 17.07.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 731 of 2021 instituted under Sections 323/498A/342/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 /4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per the complaint petition, the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the petitioner on 15.12.2018.

Thereafter, she went to her matrimonial house and as per the allegation, the in-laws started torturing her for bringing an additional dowry of Rs. 5,00,000/- and on non- fulfilment of the said demand, she was physically and mentally tortured.
In the meantime, the complainant became pregnant and gave birth to a female child.
The newly born child was very weak and was admitted to Bokaro General Hospital but due to illness, she died.
The husband of the complainant refused to deposit the hospital bill.
The parents of the complainant deposited the bill of the hospital.
It is further alleged that the complainant was ousted by her husband and her in-laws from her matrimonial house.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and will not indulge in tampering with prosecution evidence and will abide by all terms and conditions imposed by this Court in the matter Sudhanshu Kumar Soni vs The State Of Jharkhand on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121967063/
1 of granting anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P. appearing for the State as well as the learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
It appears that it is a complaint case lodged by the complainant and it also appears that the dispute could not be settled between the parties.
There is no necessity of custodial trial of the petitioner.
Hence, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, this anticipatory bail application is disposed off.

Petitioner is directed to seek regular bail before learned trial Court which shall be disposed off on its own merits in strict compliance with the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation &
Anr. reported in 2021(10) SCC 773.
